title: Prove Venus as a thin native client for Orbit
description: Prove the smallest useful native graphical materializer for one accepted Orbit session while preserving Orbit as the sole PTY and terminal authority. The initial experiment is one local Linux window, one active client, exact Orbit contract consumption, and no workspace feature expansion.
design:
Orbit governance gate orb-9o6 is closed, and the user activated ven-upt.1 as the sole Orbit/Venus/Astra architecture and research frontier. Product implementation remains deferred. The separate repository boundary is deliberate: Orbit owns terminal authority and wire interpretation, Venus owns graphical materialization, and Astra owns product orchestration and workspace policy.

ven-upt.1 evaluates the backend and composition shape against the accepted Orbit presentation codec at 6e53fedb97f764f3683c83edcd9a5227b8f56e56. Before it can complete, the missing reusable attach, semantic-input, and resize codec must return to Orbit and the user for an explicit boundary decision. If the user later accepts the complete decision and activates ven-upt.2, that Bead implements one bounded Linux slice. Venus never compensates with a mirror schema; graphical code never enters Orbit, and Astra implementation remains deferred.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The user activates the Venus architecture decision after the Orbit governance handoff.
2. Every implementation Bead follows the Execution baseline, Reference gate, Crate gate when triggered, contract-proof, portability, and closure rules in AGENTS.md.
3. VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 are either proved at exact accepted commits or retain explicit gaps.
4. Venus records every exact consumed Orbit proof revision and reports boundary gaps to Orbit rather than adding a second terminal or protocol owner.
5. The first client proves one useful Linux window, semantic interaction, reconnect, and bounded failure UX without expanding into workspace features.
6. No known P0 or P1 correctness risk remains unrecorded at the experiment decision boundary.
notes: Orbit prerequisite orb-9o6 is satisfied, and ven-upt.1 is active. ven-upt.2 remains deferred until the user accepts the protocol, backend, and composition decision and explicitly activates product implementation. Orbit orb-bi4.4 tracks cross-repository acceptance; Venus owns its production code and proof. Separate repositories and histories preserve ownership, forkability, and experimentation. This epic changes no Orbit contract and does not activate Astra.

title: Choose the minimum Venus backend and composition shape
description: Before any Cargo manifest or graphical implementation, choose the smallest backend, composition, text, and renderer ownership shape that can prove VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 against the accepted Orbit frame contract.
design:
Before any Cargo manifest or graphical implementation, pin Orbit presentation proofs ORB-C4 and ORB-C6 plus canonical orbit-protocol 0.1.0 at 6e53fedb97f764f3683c83edcd9a5227b8f56e56, and semantic-input behavior ORB-C5 at e4fde443e625180d7332eff4dff366f64bee30a8. The Orbit-owned presentation decoder and reducer are accepted. The remaining protocol blocker is the private attach, server-outcome, semantic-input, paste, and resize syntax: resolve it through an explicit user-approved Orbit boundary rather than mirroring it in Venus.

Complete the required reference gate over the exact Orbit proofs; FrankenTUI presenter-emission, terminal-backend, backend-strategy, deterministic backend, and test surfaces; OpenTUI Rust composition; Ghostling; and libghostty-rs. Then run the crate gate over complete credible native shapes: winit plus wgpu and glyphon or cosmic-text; a compatible libghostty-derived renderer boundary; Sugarloaf only if a named need activates it; another maintained native stack found in the gate; and the smallest credible owned or no-new-dependency shape. Compare deterministic state-to-draw ownership, Unicode and graphemes, cursor, clipping and layering, native input, accessibility, Linux behavior, macOS feasibility, browser implications, LOC, dependency and Nix cost, maintenance, license, and security. Stop for user choice before a manifest edit.
acceptance_criteria:
1. An Execution baseline states that this is a research and dependency decision and changes no product contract by itself.
2. The decision records ORB-C4 and ORB-C6 proof 6e53fedb97f764f3683c83edcd9a5227b8f56e56, ORB-C5 proof e4fde443e625180d7332eff4dff366f64bee30a8, the canonical protocol owners, and the exact-revision distribution shape before Venus schema or manifest edits.
3. Venus does not handwrite or generate an independent mirror. The missing reusable local-session codec returns to Orbit and the user rather than becoming a Venus adapter or fourth repository.
4. The Reference gate records exact identities and evidence from Orbit, FrankenTUI, OpenTUI Rust, Ghostling, and libghostty-rs before code-shape selection.
5. FrankenTUI supplies only backend, deterministic transition, and test-architecture lessons; OpenTUI Rust supplies only composition lessons; rejected TUI, widget, terminal-output, runtime, copied-source, and incompatible-license scope is explicit.
6. The Crate gate compares complete credible ownership shapes, including the smallest owned or no-new-dependency shape where credible, with exact versions and measured or focused evidence.
7. The decision recommends one native shape with owner boundaries, expected LOC, dependency footprint, portability disposition, first contract check, migration risk, and rollback condition.
8. No Cargo manifest, production decoder, renderer, compatibility layer, general UI framework, or Orbit distribution surface is added before explicit user approval.
notes: Required routing: docs/REFERENCES.md#required-before-the-first-client-implementation. Orbit protocol ownership and the Jeffrey Emanuel reference inspection are recorded; Ghostling, libghostty-rs, the local-session boundary decision, and the crate comparison remain open. The first proof should expose exactly equal deterministic scene state through a headless boundary before manual window dogfood. Naming a crate does not select it.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Protocol-consumption decision gate (2026-08-04): STOP before the remaining renderer reference/crate gate and before any schema or manifest edit. Exact source inspection at accepted Orbit proof e4fde443e625180d7332eff4dff366f64bee30a8 found one publish=false binary package only; ORBF v1 constants and Encoder are private in src/presentation.rs, while Decoder and decode_frame exist only inside its cfg(test) module. There is no library target, reusable canonical decoder/reducer, generated binding, schema artifact, approved package, or exact-revision distribution surface. Current Orbit governance HEAD 10a24532c00a8ea11f90055f6ce20858146e42d0 preserves that product surface. Therefore a Venus decoder would be a forbidden handwritten mirror and acceptance criteria 2-3 require returning to Orbit orb-bi4.4 for explicit user choice. Recommended smallest ownership shape: add one platform-neutral, dependency-free Orbit-owned protocol workspace package that contains ORBF version/bounds, canonical decode/validation, and revision reduction semantics; Orbit server and Venus both consume it, and Venus pins the exact Orbit Git revision for the first slice. This avoids a fourth repository, crates.io publication, generated copies, private libghostty state, and pulling Orbit server/libghostty/libc dependencies into Venus. Credible rejected shapes: a Venus-owned decoder or copied source (second owner); schema/codegen tooling (broader unproved surface); recorded frames alone (evidence, not interpretation); and a library target in the existing server package unless feature surgery proves it does not drag Linux/libghostty build ownership into Venus. Required user decision: approve or reject the recommended new Orbit workspace package plus exact-Git-revision consumption surface. No Reference gate is claimed yet; required renderer sources remain unread for this run until this ownership gate resolves.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Protocol-consumption recheck (2026-08-04): the accepted Orbit follow-up package at proof 6e53fedb97f764f3683c83edcd9a5227b8f56e56 successfully makes ORBF v1 Frame values, strict bounded decode, encode, and FrameReducer canonical in orbit-protocol, with Venus intended to consume the exact Git revision. A complete client-boundary inspection nevertheless found a separate remaining ownership gap: attach status and FRAME length envelopes, request/response lines, and all semantic input/resize syntax remain private in Orbit src/main.rs and src/presentation.rs. The current socket parser recognizes only KEY UP, KEY ENTER, focus, three mouse buttons, line-delimited PASTE, and RESIZE; line-delimited paste cannot carry embedded newlines, and there is no canonical reusable transport/request codec. Venus therefore cannot prove VEN-C2 or VEN-C4 without copying private protocol syntax, and the current key subset cannot support ordinary native text entry correctly. This is not repaired by the ORBF decoder and must not be hidden in Venus. Completing ven-upt.1 now requires a user-approved Orbit boundary decision: recommend one versioned, bounded, dependency-free, typed local-session codec in the existing orbit-protocol package for attach/frame envelopes, server outcomes, complete semantic key events, mouse/focus/paste/resize requests, and exact-revision compatibility. Orbit remains the sole terminal-aware encoder; Venus maps native events only into protocol-owned semantic values. This expands/hardens ORB-C5 and the client-visible ORB-C3/ORB-C4 boundary, so AGENTS.md requires explicit user approval before creating the Orbit implementation Bead or changing those contracts. No Venus docs, manifest, source, tests, or product contract were changed by this finding.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text:
Reference gate — Jeffrey Emanuel rendering sources (2026-08-04): required source inspection completed for VEN-C1 through VEN-C4. Exact identities: Dicklesworthstone/frankentui at 479436597890a14e82676d0067e3917b2a9de8f5 and Dicklesworthstone/opentui_rust at a37bed1d2569fdd5d3bc33ec19c0678cd0cb1cd8. Read each complete AGENTS.md and README, then inspected FrankenTUI ADR-002, ADR-003, ADR-005, ADR-008, ADR-009; crates/ftui-backend/src/lib.rs; ftui-render Buffer, DoubleBuffer, BufferDiff, Frame, HeadlessTerm, and property/headless tests; ftui-web StepProgram, WebPresenter, patch formation, and the browser-owned frame loop. Inspected OpenTUI Rust OptimizedBuffer, ScissorStack, OpacityStack, draw-buffer composition, BufferDiff, Renderer present/resize/invalidate and layer paths, front/back hit grids, the application-owned loop, golden tests, and diff properties.

Independently useful mechanisms: keep platform event/time ownership separate from presentation; reduce accepted authoritative state through one deterministic composition path; retain a current candidate and last successfully presented state; publish interaction geometry only with the presentation revision it describes; treat resize, surface replacement, and geometry changes as explicit full-recomposition/full-redraw boundaries; keep a simple full-state fallback; use row-major deterministic ordering and reusable storage only where measured; make clipping a monotonic rectangle intersection and any approved nested opacity a clamped product; derive visual ordering and hit precedence in the same composition traversal; drive native and headless paths from the same semantic scene; prove state transitions and patch/damage invariants before optional pixel evidence. FrankenTUI ADR-009 is PROPOSED and no implemented first-party wgpu renderer was found, so its CPU instance buffer, bounded atlas, small constant draw-pass count, shared render/hit geometry, and patch-hash guidance are design hypotheses, not implementation proof. ADR-008 is also PROPOSED, although its small clock/event/presenter boundary exists and its focused tests pass.

Venus consequences: Orbit remains the only presentation and terminal-state author. Venus should materialize a complete accepted ORBF frame into one pure Venus-owned draw scene whose ordered visual inputs and hyperlink or other contract-approved hit metadata share the same Orbit revision. The native host owns window, input, surface lifecycle, and failure UX; the renderer consumes the scene and does not parse transport or terminal state. Candidate and presented scene/hit state must advance together only after successful present. Because current Orbit input is complete frames, Venus should first rebuild the scene deterministically and full redraw; local damage may be derived later from consecutive accepted scenes after measurement and must not become a second wire protocol. Initial Venus has no approved general layer, popup, widget, or alpha-composition feature, so OpenTUI stack mechanics are conditional patterns rather than new scope.

Rejected surrounding scope: all ANSI and raw-terminal presentation, VT or input parsing, terminal capability policy, TUI widgets/runtime, generic widget registries, per-project grapheme/link pools, web bridge, DOM/canvas path, threaded renderer, and direct source reuse. Also rejected for the first slice are FrankenTUI dirty-row plus dirty-span plus bitmap plus tile plus certificate machinery, adaptive resize allocation policy, Bayesian or scheduler machinery, patch transport, and an eager custom glyph atlas. OpenTUI Renderer itself is not a Venus boundary because it bundles terminal lifecycle, output, buffers, layers, pools, hit state, timing, and statistics. Its cell grid is evidence for composition semantics, not the final GPU/text representation.

First meaningful Venus check: a bounded canonical ORBF corpus reduces repeated runs to byte-for-byte identical ordered draw-scene snapshots and revision-tagged hit metadata; properties cover viewport bounds, wide head/spacer consistency, cursor and hyperlink alignment, deterministic order, stale/out-of-order revision rejection, resize invalidation, and complete fallback recomposition. Headless evidence proves state/composition only; font quality, IME, accessibility, GPU/window lifecycle, and visual quality remain manual/native proof surfaces.

Verification evidence: cargo test -p ftui-backend passed 23 tests; cargo test -p ftui-render --test headless_integration passed 5 tests; focused OpenTUI tests test_scissor_stack, test_opacity_multiply, test_present_swaps_buffers, test_renderer_hit_test_after_present, and test_merge_layers_composites_hit_grids_by_layer_id each passed. License record: both repositories carry the same nonstandard MIT rider in LICENSE at these commits while manifests label packages MIT. The user and Yazelix independently direct and benefit from this architectural inspection and are not placed within the named on-behalf-of, for-benefit-of, or under-direction condition merely by tool choice. This gate authorizes research conclusions only: no code was copied or adapted, no dependency or source reuse was selected, and redistribution or incorporation remains a separate gate.

comments.author: lucca
comments.text: Reference gate addendum — grapheme fidelity: FrankenTUI ftui-web cell_to_patch at 479436597890a14e82676d0067e3917b2a9de8f5 maps every pooled grapheme to the literal square fallback code point before host or GPU transfer. Its current 16-byte patch cell therefore cannot preserve arbitrary grapheme content and is not a usable Venus wire, scene, text, or fidelity proof. Venus must retain the exact Orbit-authored grapheme identity through deterministic scene construction into the selected shaper and renderer; damage metadata may point at changed draw inputs but must never replace text content with a renderer-local placeholder. This reinforces rejecting the FrankenTUI patch schema while retaining only its bounded contiguous-run and full-repaint concepts if later measurement activates local damage.

title: Render one accepted Orbit session in a minimum Linux window
description: Implement the smallest Venus slice: one Linux window consumes canonical structured frames from an already-running Orbit session, renders their accepted rich state, sends semantic input and resize, remains transient across client exit, and explains bounded attachment or server failure.
design:
Begin only after the user activates Venus, accepts the backend and composition decision, and accepts one exact-revision canonical Orbit protocol-consumption shape. Pin the exact accepted Orbit commit and ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 states. Decode accepted ORBF v1 complete frames into one persistent Venus PresentationState before producing draw inputs; reconnect and resync replace that state coherently. This keeps a later user-approved patch protocol compatible with the same reducer model without implementing patches now.

Before manual window dogfood, use a bounded canonical frame corpus or the smallest protocol-faithful source to prove deterministic decode and frame-to-draw inputs without a live PTY, handwritten mirror schema, raw VT parser, or second terminal authority. Keep Linux window and GPU mechanics inside Venus and report any protocol gap to Orbit through separate owner commits and compatibility sequencing.
acceptance_criteria:
1. The user activates Venus, Orbit orb-9o6 is closed, and the accepted protocol-consumption plus backend and composition decisions are recorded before implementation.
2. The Execution baseline records the exact Orbit proof commit, consumed ORB-C1 through ORB-C7 states, affected VEN-C1 through VEN-C4 contracts, intended surfaces, and pre-existing worktree state.
3. The pre-code Reference gate and accepted Crate gate satisfy AGENTS.md; manifest changes match the user-approved protocol and dependency shapes exactly.
4. A focused nonvisual check consumes canonical Orbit ORBF v1 frames, applies complete frames and ordered revisions to one bounded persistent PresentationState, and deterministically produces draw inputs for styled Unicode and graphemes, cursor, alternate screen, reconnect, and failure cases.
5. One Linux window attaches to an already-running Orbit session, renders coherent current state, and sends semantic keyboard input and resize through Orbit.
6. Closing or crashing Venus leaves Orbit and the PTY alive; reopening receives and applies coherent current state.
7. Attach rejection, incompatible or invalid frames, revision failures, and Orbit loss produce clear bounded failures rather than hangs or invented state.
8. Venus owns no PTY, terminal emulator, terminal-query response, raw VT parser, mirrored protocol schema, terminal history content, workspace topology, or Astra policy.
9. Closure records deterministic checks, manual visual dogfood, owned LOC, dependency footprint, portability disposition, exact Orbit compatibility, proof revisions, and remaining gaps.
10. Patches, history pages, ordered terminal effects, richer resources, tabs, panes, sidebars, popups, settings, visual effects, configuration, plugins, remote or web access, macOS implementation, packaging, and distribution remain excluded.
notes: Required references and classifications are in docs/REFERENCES.md. Orbit orb-bi4.4 is the cross-repository acceptance tracker; this Bead is the sole owner of Venus implementation. A required new Orbit trace format, command, package, adapter, or compatibility window returns for explicit user choice.
